scope: Read all thirteen passages, overview, periods, ending and source notes. Independently checked all six cited sources for the writing sample, selected household and food claims, settlement interpretation and political transition. This is a bounded source review, not independent archaeological reanalysis or a review of every underlying reference in the six works.

checkedSources.access: Direct English Heritage announcement text, dated 15 June 2018.
checkedSources.result: Exact Latin phrase viri duo and translation two men verified. Seventh-century date, slate window ledge, Latin/Greek/Christian marks, mixed book/document lettering and possible writing practice all supported. No original-inscription image inspection claimed.
Greek amphorae, local slate stoppers with beeswax, probable southern French glass and probable post-Roman quern all supported with appropriate qualifiers.

checkedSources.access: Full original report text; printed pages 17 and 93 to 95, human PDF pages 28 and 104 to 106.
checkedSources.result: Post-Roman Geraint midden 505 includes barley, naked wheat and a few oat grains. Printed page 94 explicitly distinguishes these from medieval Tristan deposits and discusses cleaned/threshed grain, nearby supply and alternative sprouting explanations. Card does not misattribute medieval oats or claim proven brewing.

Fresh water, hearths, narrow defensible approach, approximate 450 to 650 prosperity and probable itinerant royal use supported. Earlier site dates are distinguished from the map interval and kingdom lifetime. Arthurian attribution is correctly much later.
Approximately one hundred buildings, uncertain functions, southern paving/steps and alternative function of the thick eastern wall all match the source.

checkedSources.access: Full Nicholas Grant article text in the Devon Historian 79 PDF; printed pages 19 to 24 and notes.
checkedSources.result: Aldhelm's letter addresses Geraint and bishops; date is uncertain within 682 to 706, with Grant favoring the later end. The card's approximate opening-of-eighth-century wording is defensible. Chronicle's 710 entry gives no result; later John of Worcester adds flight. Devon/Cornwall transition is carefully stated without a invented final event.

independentSourceBudget.method: Unicode word count; overview, canonical summary, period titles and summaries, passages and ending charged fully to every cited source; no aliases or duplicate URLs present.
